# The full integer slot lattice is generated by physical strong sources

**Proved.** For every order n≥5, the additive group generated by the
differences of the optional-slot polynomials of strong n-tournaments
is exactly

    2 Z z^δ + 2 Z z^(δ+2) + ... + 2 Z z^(n−2),
    δ = 1 for odd n, 2 for even n.

This is a statement about signed combinations of profiles. It does
not say every admissible vector is individually realizable or provide
an absolute-target source. In particular the matching-section rank
bound is sharp even on the affine span of actual strong profiles. No
further universal affine linear congruence of their full polynomial
coordinates is possible beyond those of this explicit lattice.

## 1. The ambient lattice and physically supplied basis

The disjoint odd-cycle packing formula gives monic degree n, parity
n, zero constant for n>0, and even coefficients below the leading
term. Let M_n denote the integral lower-coefficient space with basis
z^δ,z^(δ+2),...,z^(n−2); divide all differences by 2.

Without a strongness restriction the divided difference lattice is
already all of M_n. Compare TT_n with the near-transitive R_j, a
transitive chain on j+2 vertices with the extreme arc reversed,
padded by a transitive ordinal segment to order n. Every directed
cycle in R_j uses that one reverse arc, and an odd cycle of length
2k+1 chooses 2k−1 inner vertices. The divided differences are

    Σ_(k≥1) binom(j,2k−1) z^(n−2k).

Take j=1,3,...,2 floor((n−1)/2)−1. At each new j the new coefficient
is one and all lower terms vanish, a triangular integral basis.
The empty basis is interpreted conventionally.

## 2. Strongening with a singleton cycle wrap

At fixed p≥1 make S=C3[U,TT_p,1], using U→TT_p→x→U. It is strong.
Its slot polynomial is L_p(Q_U), where for a polynomial f,

    L_p f = z^(p+1) f
          + z((z+1)^p−z^p)(f(z+1)−f(z))
          + z((z−1)^p−z^p)(f(z−1)−f(z)).

Indeed an odd-cycle packing entirely inside U contributes the first
term. A cycle using two modules must use all three, including x, so
there is only one such cycle in a packing. Reading it from x selects
one nonempty path in U and one in the transitive module; the two path
orders must sum to an even number so that the total length including x
is odd. Their vertices are removed from the original slot polys and
a factor 2z records the new cycle. In detail, the identities

    Q_U(z±1) = Σ_(D⊆U) (±1)^|D| H(U[D]) Q_(U−D)(z)

follow from assigning slots in two bands (binomial convolution) and
Q_U(−1)=(−1)^n H(U). Subtracting the empty selections and summing the
two products keeps exactly twice the even-parity pairs, giving the
formula. All other cycles are in U and disjoint from the selected path.

For p=1 the formula becomes z²f+z(f(z+1)−f(z−1)). Its image
L_1 M_(n−2) is a saturated, codimension-one subgroup of M_n:
each monomial maps to a monic next-degree monomial plus lower terms.
Eliminate the highest degree repeatedly by these image elements.
The sole remainder is λ(g) z^δ. This defines an integer functional
with kernel L_1 M_(n−2); modulo two, λ(g) is just the coefficient
of z^δ, as all lower terms of L_1 on monomials are even.
All this image lattice is generated by divided differences of literal
strong order-n profiles, using the unconditioned source basis above.

## 3. The primitive leftover, odd orders

For odd n≥7, z² belongs to M_(n−3). The p=2 wrap supplies L_2(z²)
as an integer combination of divided strong differences. The identity

    L_2(z²)−L_1(z³+2z) = −4z

shows a residual −4. Now compare the near-transitive R_(n−2), with
one directed Hamilton cycle, and the regular cyclic tournament C5
with one vertex replaced by TT_(n−4). The regular order-five
tournament with arrows i→i+1,i+2 modulo five has exactly two
directed Hamilton cycles, the +1 and +2 cycles, checked with a
fixed start among its 24 remaining vertex orders.

Replacing a single vertex of a tournament by a nonempty uniform
module preserves the parity of Hamilton-cycle counts when at least
one old exterior vertex remains. Start each cycle at one exterior
vertex. A collapsed cyclic word visiting the module k times is
filled by an ordered k-path cover, whose count is divisible by k!;
there is no division by k or by the cycle length because the start
is fixed outside. Thus only k=1 matters modulo two, and its
multiplicative factor H(U) is odd by Rédei. In our comparison the
inflated regular C5 therefore still has an even cycle count and is
strong. The divided z coefficient is exactly the difference of
Hamilton-cycle counts, since a cycle packing yields z exponent one
only for a single Hamilton cycle. This residual is odd. Together
with −4 it generates Z.

## 4. The primitive leftover, even orders

For even n≥10, z³ and z⁵ both belong to M_(n−3). In the even
parity quotient their p=2 wraps have residuals

    λ(L_2 z³) = −14,    λ(L_2 z⁵) = 114.

For example L_2 z³=z⁶+12z⁴+10z²; subtract L_1 z⁴=z⁶+8z⁴+8z²,
then subtract 4L_1 z²=4z⁴+16z². For z⁵, subtract L_1 z⁶ from
z⁸+20z⁶+60z⁴+14z² to get 8z⁶+20z⁴+2z²; eliminate z⁶ and z⁴ in
the same way, leaving 114z². Their gcd is two.

An odd residual comes from the difference of C3[TT_(n−3),TT_2,1]
and R_(n−2). The divided coefficient of z² modulo two counts
cycles of length n−1: a packing with two disjoint covering odd
cycles also contributes to z², but its weight divided by two
is even. In the triangle wrap, to make a cycle of length n−1
omit one vertex from one of the two transitive modules (there
are n−3 and 2 choices, respectively). Each choice gives precisely
one one-round cycle; omitting the singleton gives none. Thus there
are n−1 such cycles, odd. In R_(n−2) there are n−2, even. This odd
residual and the two even residues generate Z.

At n=8, z³ supplies −14. The divided difference of the two
transitive wraps is

    (L_2 z⁵ − L_1 z⁶)/2 = 4z⁶+10z⁴+z²,

with residual 57. The gcd of 14 and 57 is one.

At n=5 the literal strong profiles (H,Q2)=(9,84),(11,100),(13,104)
have pair-difference determinant −24; the conversion from normalized
two-degree coefficients to (H,Q2) also has determinant −24. At n=6
the corresponding triple is (15,216),(17,224),(19,256), determinant
48, while the conversion has determinant −48. Thus both bases are
saturated. Orders three and four are intentionally excluded: each
has just one strong tournament type, while the ambient affine
dimension is one.

Combining with the p=1 image, all residual Z is generated in every
claimed order, proving the integral span. The operational limits
are important: no signed affine basis itself supplies a realization
of a desired point, just as low-degree cohomology of a hyperplane
section doesn't reconstruct the whole original object.
